Default-off direct block adoption is implemented and passes CPU validation: 174 extension tests plus 13 selected native prefix-cache regressions. CUDA stayed uninitialized. No GPU correctness test, model loading, inference, CUDA build or performance measurement ran for this continuation. The earlier screen in ../REPORT.md is preserved and does not measure adoption.

Enable with `wait_hint_native_adoption=true`; false remains the default. Support is deliberately restricted to dense causal BF16, TP1, one group and one hash per block, with a complete previously observed exact prefix. Other layouts, incomplete completion evidence, identity mismatch, disabled prefix lookup and missing runtime support retain the existing path.

After successful transfer completion from every contributor and exact returning-request binding, the connector publishes its reserved physical blocks under the native request hash chain. `BlockPool.publish_completed_prefix` validates every pool object, reference, hash and group before mutation, then consumes the reservation references. Native cache lookup and allocation attach those same objects to request block tables. Publication is evictable and distinct from actual adoption. There is no prefix destination allocation or GPU splice in the adopted path; the mutable suffix still allocates normally. If pressure evicts the publication before admission, ordinary demand restoration supplies the missing prefix. Cancellation or expiry while transfers are in flight cannot recycle destinations before completion. Published immutable data follows native sharing/refcount/eviction rules.

The 30 new parametrized cases use the actual recovered BlockPool, KVCacheManager, Request hashing, connector request registration and connector-aware native lookup. They verify identical physical IDs, suffix-only allocation, no splice/demand load on adoption, exact BF16 CPU tensor contents, two-request sharing, capacity/refcount invariants, pressure, in-flight/ready expiry and cancellation, failed/duplicate completion, key reordering, whole-prefix rejection, publication rollback and unsupported/default guards. Completion events are injected: actual CUDA transfer fences, worker block-table installation and generated-output exactness are unverified. The native regression subset covers reuse, eviction, held references, disabled caching, reset and cache events.

Evidence: evidence/validation.json; evidence/extension-cpu-summary.json; evidence/native-cpu-summary.json; final activity receipts contain complete stdout and empty-owned-tree evidence. Earlier failed attempts are retained: an initial test-runner guard alias conflicted with Torch Dynamo registration; a demand-fallback assertion used the wrong job-map key; expanding through real request registration exposed a missing fixture lifecycle setting. These test preparation issues were repaired. The final suites pass. AST syntax, whitespace and reverse patch-application checks pass; Ruff/pre-commit were unavailable in the retained environment and were not installed.

Patches for Mac integration:
- extension-adoption-delta.patch: adoption changes relative to baseline/connector.py and baseline/test_step_1_5_prefetch.py, excluding the preexisting matched-control diagnostic flag.
- extension-full.patch: complete extension diff against original source HEAD, including that prior flag. Choose full OR delta according to the destination state.
- runtime-adoption.patch: new native publication API against the recovered runtime baseline.

Exact source/runtime identities, baseline hashes and final file/patch hashes are in evidence/baseline.json and evidence/implementation-pins.json. Runtime is the recovered authoritative Python subset plus pinned wheel additions, not the exact historical full Git tree. ../evidence/environment-freeze.txt, runtime-stage.json, recovered-runtime-files.json and runtime-overlay.json retain environment/recovery provenance. Parent integrates; no commit, push or PR was created.

Native Windows quiet custody initially blocked all CPU testing, including light admission. Only after that owner released did the broker offer and accept this finite CPU-only light reservation. Testing used mediated launches, one CPU affinity/thread, CUDA-init guards, offline access, a finite timeout and the existing nonblocking project lock. No quiet grant was requested. The GPU remains untested by explicit task choice under the timing-sensitive-job constraint, even after CPU admission became available. No performance benefit, removal of the earlier 40–56 ms interval, or prior-result reproduction is claimed.

Cleanup and retained inventory: evidence/storage-handback.json and evidence/cleanup.json. The no-child parent brief prevented delegated inventory; the operational owner performed the bounded pass. Useful recovery archives, source, environment, prior raw results and shared model/dependency caches remain preserved. No personal/host settings changed or historical campaign resumed.

Handback verified: all owned activity trees empty, project lock free, source/runtime hashes intact, sealed restoration succeeded and native authority released the reservation. Finite keeper stopped, read-only offer wait exited and offer subscription cancelled. New adoption artifacts occupy approximately 0.94 MB; only 2 KB of exact redundant console receipts were removed. The reusable environment (~8.0GB), recovered runtime (~0.79GB), recovery inputs (~0.32GB) and prior compressed results (~0.26GB) remain preserved; these are prior handback sizes. Current WSL free space was approximately 7.16 GB, affected by concurrent work. Windows storage was untouched by this continuation.
